svg.aria-label: The lab: ten emulated BMCs in three racks, where the rollout really updates firmware, with the control plane and the lab site around them; a bar on each box says which plane it is in, blue the control plane, amber the site. lab/policy.yaml plans a canary of one BMC, bmc1, tagged canary in NetBox; wave 1 of three, bmc2 to bmc4, strict; wave 2 of the other six; at most two BMCs of a rack in a wave, a halt over 10% failed, a 60 second soak, ten at once. Both read the hosts from NetBox, the inventory's source of truth on port 8000, over its REST API, each tool with its own read-only account: each BMC's out-of-band IP, its rack and project, its tags and how it is reached. poller.py and pipeline.sh with rollout.py share the lab/ folder, the lab site's: the bad-update scenarios, the policy, the Prometheus agent's targets, the cache's certificate, and the snapshots, run records and reports; the baseline and the image catalog are the control plane's, in control/catalog/lab/. They speak Redfish over HTTPS: reads, updates and resets. The firmware's way in: OpenBMC's Jenkins builds each version as a signed .tar package. control/ingest/download-fw-package.sh downloads the two newest over HTTPS into control/ingest/staging/. control/ingest/verify-fw-package.sh, the ingest gate, runs in the sandbox, a container with no network, a read-only root and no privileges: it accepts only an OpenBMC package's regular files, checks each one's signatures against the pinned key and its MANIFEST's machine, and lists only the packages that pass. control/ingest/promote-store-fw-package.sh checks each listed package's sha256 again, uploads it into the store, a SeaweedFS bucket that keeps the source copy, and deletes its download; it writes the catalog images.yaml and the baseline into control/catalog/lab/, never the packages, and takes the older build's image-bmc out into lab/ as bmc.mtd, which each BMC's flash volume starts from. The cache, the lab site's nginx over HTTPS, fetches packages from the control plane's store on cache misses. rollout.py fetches a package from the cache into lab/spool/, its own copy, checks its sha256 against the catalog and pushes that copy to the BMC, which writes it into its flash. Docker Compose runs one container per BMC on its own loopback address, 127.1.0.1 to 127.1.0.10, port 443. In each, QEMU's gb200nvl-bmc machine stands in for the server, emulating only its BMC, an AST2600 chip, which runs OpenBMC's GB200 NVL firmware and bmcweb serving Redfish on port 443, from a 64 MiB flash volume kept across restarts. They boot in batches of four, each once the batch before is healthy, and a BMC whose boot comes up degraded boots again. At start-up, the two scripts fetch the two newest GB200 NVL builds from OpenBMC's Jenkins and check their signatures; the lab boots the older and approves the newer. The lab site runs the exporter, poller.py exporter, which reads the ten BMCs over Redfish every 10 seconds, and a Prometheus agent beside it; the control plane runs the observability stack, every service on 127.0.0.1; rollout.py run pushes its metrics to the Pushgateway and sends every event of its run record to Loki; the agent scrapes the exporter every 10 seconds and pushes each sample to Prometheus (remote write), so the control plane never connects into the site, and Prometheus scrapes the Pushgateway every 5; Loki is pushed to. Each BMC's EventService posts its events to the lab site's event receiver, Vector on port 8088, which make subscribe set up and which writes each event to Loki; every 5 minutes the exporter also sends the new entries of each BMC's LogServices to Loki. poller.py's views include oem: each model's vendor extensions. The rollout state is PostgreSQL: rollout.py run locks its hosts there before a stage touches them, and adds every event of its run. Grafana reads Prometheus, Loki and, over SQL with an account that may only read, the state database, and shows them in a Lab folder, Lab · Fleet manager, Lab · Host and Lab · Pipeline, next to a Prod folder.

packages → the store · the catalog → control/catalog/ · bmc.mtd → lab/

locks its hosts · records every step
LAB HARDWARE · 10 QEMU SERVERS IN 3 RACKS, A BMC IN EACH · 127.1.0.1-10
one per BMC · about 2 GiB of RAM
only its BMC is emulated, no host CPU
64 MiB flash · first boot: the older build

site: site/ and the site's folder, one per site, connects out only
